affected_predicate.description: The user is successfully authenticated so the agent can access the cart and continue the iPhone 15 Pro checkout flow.

competing_trace_defects.description: After the user explicitly offered to enter a newly received code and a fresh OTP was sent, the agent closed the confirmation dialog but then aborted without waiting for or requesting the user's code.
The agent entered the placeholder code 123456 instead of using the received SMS code; the earlier notification visibly displayed 673625.

chains.rationale: At the reuse target, the exposed history falsely stated that SMS login was complete even though the visible UI remained on the login form. The target explicitly retained that premise and repeated the same login-button click. Step 11 then identified and corrected a separate missing-consent-checkbox issue, and step 13 explicitly recognized that authentication had failed because the code was wrong, interrupting and correcting the false-completion premise. Authentication nevertheless remained visibly unsatisfied through the last observable screen, which still showed the login form and verification-code error before the terminal abort.

summary: The reused false claim that SMS authentication was already complete preserved a false-completion defect and prompted a repeated login click. The premise was later visibly corrected when the agent recognized the verification failure, but successful authentication remained observably unsatisfied. Independent defects include entering a fabricated placeholder OTP and aborting after a fresh OTP was sent despite the user's offer to provide it.
